reviewer: CI unblock — committed static server (guardian #7 postmortem fix)
note: guardian #7 (eb18192, Nov 6) failed and blocked the Pages deploy: launch-check's lighthouse sub-check could not start a server in CI because _serve.mjs was a local-only scratch file that was never committed — and the same push gitignored _*.mjs, making it uncommittable. The local GO baselines (D5) ran where _serve.mjs existed. Fix: added scripts/serve.mjs (dependency-free node:http static server, port 4174, committed), pointed lighthouserc.json and scripts/lighthouse-check.mjs at it, and replaced the execSync server bootstrap with spawn (a server never exits; execSync would hang). Lesson: CI must never depend on uncommitted scratch files; the .gitignore pattern that excludes them makes it structural. Second bug found in the same mechanism while verifying the fix in CI: the ensureServer readiness probe called net.createConnection(host, port) with the arguments swapped — a string first argument is treated as an IPC socket path, so the probe failed even when the server was up (this is why run #8/#9 still failed at server-start after the server fix). Replaced the probe with an HTTP fetch. Also: launch-check now prints the tail of a failed sub-check output (previously execSync captured and discarded it, making CI failures undiagnosable), and npx --yes pins the Lighthouse install prompt. CI structure improvement (de-dup): the guard job previously ran a11y/lighthouse/verify-live twice per run — once inside launch-check (execSync-captured, invisible on failure) and once as separate steps. Now the standalone steps run first (full per-step logs) and launch-check runs --ready-only in CI, skipping the duplicated re-run (locally it still runs everything). Failed launch-check sub-checks also emit GitHub ::error:: annotations so the reason is readable on the run page even when step logs are truncated. Third finding (run #12): once the probe worked, Lighthouse itself failed in CI with "waiting for dynamic debugging port" — chrome-launcher starts Chrome without sandbox flags and it dies on the runner. Fix: --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage" (standard for CI; local runs keep working). Fourth finding (run #15, annotations): with Chrome launching, the budget step failed with error-level "audit not found in report" — lighthouserc.json asserted the "interactive" (TTI) audit, which was removed from Lighthouse v10+. Fix: dropped the interactive assertion (TBT already covers main-thread blocking); the rest of the budget is untouched. Fifth finding (run #15, annotations title "lighthouse:dom-size"): with the sandbox and TTI fixes in, Lighthouse ran and every budget passed except dom-size — the dom-size audit was replaced by the "Optimize DOM size" insight in Lighthouse 13 (Oct 2025) and no longer exists in the report at all. Removed the assertion; the insight variant has no comparable node-count numericValue, and the site DOM is small enough that the performance category budget (>= 90) already covers regression.
